response.sql: WITH per_account AS (SELECT account_id, COUNT(*) AS order_cnt FROM "order" GROUP BY account_id), shares AS (SELECT account_id, order_cnt, CAST(order_cnt AS REAL) / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM "order") AS share FROM per_account), avg_share AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS avg_s FROM shares) SELECT SUM(s.order_cnt) AS total_orders, AVG(s.share) AS avg_share, AVG(s.share - a.avg_s) AS avg_excess_over_average FROM shares s CROSS JOIN avg_share a WHERE s.share > a.avg_s

assumptions.assumption: Total number of orders is the row count of the order table; every order row belongs to an account in the table, so shares sum to 1 across accounts with orders.
'How far their share is above the average share' is the mean of (share - overall average share) across the selected accounts, in absolute share units, not a percentage or ratio.
